knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: CL-R1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. After a frequentist 95 percent confidence interval for fixed parameter theta has been calculated, which interpretation is correct?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: The parameter is fixed; coverage refers to the long-run behaviour of the random interval procedure.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: A 95 percent confidence procedure has 95 percent repeated-sampling coverage under its assumptions.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Assigning posterior probability to a fixed parameter.

choices.label: The construction procedure covers theta in 95 percent of repeated samples under the model.
Given these data, theta has probability 0.95 of lying in this interval.
Ninety-five percent of sample values must lie inside the interval.
There is a 95 percent probability that the statistical model is true.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: CL-R1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. In a Normal linear model, how does a prediction interval for one future response generally compare with a confidence interval for the mean response at the same predictor value?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Prediction includes irreducible observation-level variance in addition to mean uncertainty.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: The prediction interval is wider because it covers a new response.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Using a mean-response confidence interval to predict one future observation.

choices.label: The prediction interval is wider because it includes mean-estimation uncertainty and the future observation's random variation.
The prediction interval is narrower because only one future value is considered.
The confidence interval includes future observation noise, but the prediction interval does not.
